Jordan (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need a practical plan to retire org-global admin keys in Private while keeping 3rd-party sinks working. Thoughts?
Maria (eng-security): Short answer: introduce per-org 'bridge' tokens with minting + audit. Avoid permanent global keys where possible.
Sam (eng-sre): Reality: some exporters only accept one static key. We should offer a proxy shim that holds a long-lived proxy key and mints short-lived per-org bridge tokens on behalf of the exporter.
Chris (security): Proxy is acceptable but must come with strict controls: HSM-backed proxy key, rotation policy, and limited scope for minted tokens.
Jordan (eng-platform): UX constraints: customers hate breaking changes. We need a compatibility mode that maps an existing long-lived customer key to an org-scoped proxy mapping, with telemetry showing usage.
Maria (eng-security): API contract sketch for minting:
POST /api/v1/tokens/mint
Body: { subject, org_id, scope[], ttl_seconds, requested_by }
Response: { token, expires_at, audit_id }
(we'll put the exact JSON in the RFC)
Sam (eng-sre): Implementation detail: caching for high-QPS worker pools. Proxy should cache recent bridge tokens for (org, subject, caller) for a short window (e.g., 5m) and respect token TTL.
Chris (security): Runtime header additions: X-Actor and X-Audit-Id propagated so services can link requests back to the mint event and caller.
deploy-bot: Note: feature-flag rollout scheduled; ensure canary includes Dedicated customers.
Maria (eng-security): Migration plan outline:
- Phase 1: Accept legacy keys through a shim and emit deprecation warnings.
- Phase 2: Offer tooling to exchange legacy key -> proxy-backed mapping.
- Phase 3: Require bridge tokens for new integrations, start rotation enforcement.
Jordan (eng-platform): Console needs org-level view: current proxy key status, active bridge tokens (last minted, last used), and one-click revoke for org.
Sam (eng-sre): Metrics to track: mint_count, renew_count, revoke_count, token_use_by_org, failed_mint_rate.
Chris (security): Threat modeling action: analyse proxy compromise scenarios, token binding to caller IP/subject, and limits on privileges encoded in bridge tokens.
Maria (eng-security): I'll draft the RFC with API details, compatibility matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and an operator checklist for migrations.
Jordan (eng-platform): Action items: @Maria RFC draft, @Chris threat model, @Sam proxy prototype & metrics, @Jordan Console mocks. Review next Tuesday.
Sam (eng-sre): +1 — will include perf targets for mint endpoint (P95 latency, QPS) in the doc.
Chris (security): Also add retention policy for audit events; make sure audit_id is immutable and searchable.
Jordan (eng-platform): Thanks all. Small note: ensure we limit which principals can call /tokens/mint (can_mint_bridge) and default to deny.
